name: generate_image
description: Generate a raster image from a text prompt using state-of-the-art image models. Width and height guide the aspect ratio; the model chooses a supported output size, so the image pixel dimensions may differ from the requested values. The tool returns a URL serving the raw image bytes of a PNG or JPEG image. IMPORTANT: The URL expires after 7 days. The user MUST download the image before the URL expires to keep a copy. **This is a paid feature — each call consumes Figma AI credits against the user's plan (different models have different per-call costs).** Alternatively, provide fileKey instead of planKey to generate and place the image directly in an editable Design, FigJam, or Slides file. If no editable file exists, call create_new_file first. File mode checks AI permissions and credits against the destination file. Omit nodeId to create a new image-filled frame, or provide nodeId to replace an existing image fill without resizing it. File mode returns fileKey, nodeId, model, width, and height for download_assets, without a temporary URL. Always provide exactly one of planKey (URL mode) or fileKey (placement mode); nodeId is only valid in file mode.

prompt.description: Text description of the image to generate.

model.description: Image model to use. One of: gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image, gpt-image-2.5-sunburst, gemini-3.1-flash-image. Defaults to gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image.

width.description: Requested width in pixels. Together with height, selects the closest supported aspect ratio; actual image width may differ. Default: 1024; max: 2048.

height.description: Requested height in pixels. Together with width, selects the closest supported aspect ratio; actual image height may differ. Default: 1024; max: 2048.

fileKey.description: Destination file for image placement. Provide either fileKey or planKey, never both.

nodeId.description: Existing node whose image fill should be replaced without resizing it. Omit to create a new frame.

planKey.description: Deprecated. Prefer fileKey to place the generated image in a file. Use planKey only for legacy temporary-URL generation, and never provide it together with fileKey.
